Sample is small, self-selected and media-linked, so rates are not population prevalence. Most logs are gpt-4o (81%), collected Sep 2025 to Jan 2026; findings may not describe current models. items.oneLine: Schimmelpfennig et al. (2026) run two experiments (N=3,500, ten countries): humanlike chatbot design reliably raises anthropomorphism, but trust and engagement effects vary by culture, and users judge humanlikeness by conversational cues rather than consciousness.
items.issues: Course guide calls this a "review"; it is an original two-study experimental paper. Source is an arXiv preprint (v2, Feb 2026); peer-review status not established. Country-level Study 2 subgroups (about 100 per arm) are exploratory and underpowered, yet drive the 'culturally contingent' headline. Study 2 pre-registration was not formally registered before data collection. Open-ended question asked about being human, not conscious, which likely depresses consciousness mentions. Data (2024, GPT-4o) predates current systems. Sibling readings were assessed by title and guide only, not read. Summary written from the full source text; supplementary material not available.
